tools.name: search-bookmarks
tools.title: Search Bookmarks
tools.description: Search through Safari Bookmarks and return matching entries
tools.instructions:
Searches the Safari bookmarks and returns each match with its folder.
`truncated` is true when more bookmarks match than were returned.

searchText.description:
The text to search for in the bookmarks.

@remarks Omit it to list bookmarks.

tools.name: search-history
tools.title: Search History
tools.description: Search through Safari browsing history and return matching entries
tools.instructions:
Searches the Safari browsing history, most recent visits first.
`truncated` is true when more entries match than were returned.

searchText.description:
Words to search for in page titles and URLs. Every word must match.

@remarks Omit it to return the most recently visited pages.

tools.name: search-reading-list
tools.title: Search Reading List
tools.description: Search through Safari Reading List and return matching items
tools.instructions:
Searches the Safari Reading List.
`truncated` is true when more items match than were returned.

searchText.description:
The text to search for in the reading list.

@remarks Omit it to list the reading list, most recently added first.

tools.name: add-to-reading-list
tools.title: Add to Reading List
tools.description: Add a specified URL to the Safari Reading List for later reading

url.description: The URL to add to the reading list.

tools.name: open-url
tools.title: Open URL
tools.description: Open a specified URL in Safari
tools.instructions:
Opens a URL in Safari and returns the new tab that shows it.
`verified` is true only when exactly one new tab appeared and it shows the requested site. Otherwise it is false,
with a `reason`, and `tab` is the new tab only when one could be identified.

tools.name: get-all-tabs
tools.title: Get All Tabs
tools.description: Return information about all open Safari tabs across all windows
tools.instructions:
Retrieves information about all open tabs across all Safari windows.

@returns An array of tab objects containing details about each tab, including
titles, URLs, and their location (window ID and position).

This tool is useful for getting a complete overview of all open Safari tabs,
allowing for operations on specific tabs based on their content or location.
The returned array is ordered by window ID and then by tab position.

tools.name: get-tab-contents
tools.title: Get Tab Contents
tools.description: Retrieve the text or HTML source code of a specific Safari tab
tools.instructions:
Retrieves the contents of a Safari tab, either the specified tab or the currently focused tab.
Returns either the visible text or HTML source code based on the type parameter.
`truncated` is true when the content was cut at maxLength.

windowId.description:
The window ID of the tab.

@remarks Safari windows are numbered starting from 1.

index.description:
The index of the tab within the window.

@remarks Tabs are numbered starting from 1, from left to right.

tab.description:
The tab to get the contents of.

@remarks If not provided, the currently focused/active tab will be used.

tools.name: close-tab
tools.title: Close Tab
tools.description: Close either a specific Safari tab or the currently active tab
tools.instructions:
Closes a Safari tab, either a specific tab identified by window ID and tab index,
or the currently focused tab if no specific tab is provided.
Closes exactly the tab shown in the confirmation. It fails without closing anything if that tab moved or changed
page, or if there is no matching confirmation for this call.
Returns the title and URL of the closed tab.

windowId.description:
The window ID of the tab to close.

@remarks Safari windows are numbered starting from 1.

index.description:
The index of the tab to close within the window.

@remarks Tabs are numbered starting from 1, from left to right.

tab.description:
The tab to close.

@remarks If not provided, the currently focused/active tab will be closed.

tools.name: select-tab
tools.title: Select Tab
tools.description: Switch to a specific Safari tab and bring its window to the front
tools.instructions:
Switches to a Safari tab and brings its window to the front.
Returns the selected tab. Its window becomes window 1, so window IDs from earlier results may have changed.

windowId.description:
The window ID of the tab to select.

@remarks Safari windows are numbered starting from 1, frontmost first. Use get-all-tabs to find it.

index.description:
The index of the tab to select within the window.

@remarks Tabs are numbered starting from 1, from left to right. Use get-all-tabs to find it.

tools.name: get-focused-tab
tools.title: Get Focused Tab
tools.description: Return information about the currently focused Safari tab
tools.instructions:
Retrieves information about the currently focused/active tab in Safari.

@returns An object containing details about the focused tab including its title, URL,
window ID, and position within the window.

This tool is useful for quickly identifying which tab the user is currently viewing
without having to search through all tabs.

scripts.prepublishOnly:
echo "

It seems like you are trying to publish the Raycast extension to npm.

If you did intend to publish it to npm, remove the \`prepublishOnly\` script and rerun \`npm publish\` again.
If you wanted to publish it to the Raycast Store instead, use \`npm run publish\` instead.

" && exit 1

ai.instructions:
Safari is Apple's web browser. A tab is identified by windowId and index, both starting at 1: windowId 1 is the frontmost window and index counts tabs from left to right. Take them from get-all-tabs or get-focused-tab and never invent them. For the current tab ("this tab", "this page"), call get-tab-contents or close-tab without a tab instead of looking up its position.
Use search-history for pages the user visited, search-bookmarks for saved bookmarks and search-reading-list for the Reading List. Only pass searchText when the user names something to look for, and keep it to the essential keywords. Pass searchLimit only when the user asks for a number of results. When a search result has truncated: true, say that more matches exist and offer to narrow the search.
If a search tool reports that Raycast needs Full Disk Access, tell the user how to grant it instead of retrying.
Use select-tab to switch to a tab. It brings that tab's window to the front, so the window becomes window 1 and other window IDs shift: call get-all-tabs again before reusing window IDs from earlier results.
open-url only opens http and https addresses. Pass the address as the user wrote it, including any port such as localhost:3000; do not add or change the scheme. It returns verified: true only when exactly one new tab opened on the requested site, and that tab is the one returned. If it returns verified: false, tell the user the reason it gives instead of claiming the page opened.
Use get-tab-contents to read a page before summarizing it or answering questions about it. Use type "source" only when the user asks about the HTML. When the user asks for only part of a page, such as the first 500 characters, pass that number as maxLength. If the result has truncated: true, say that the answer is based on the beginning of the page. If get-tab-contents reports that the page is still loading or has no text, tell the user instead of guessing what the page says.
If select-tab, close-tab or get-tab-contents reports that a tab does not exist, or that it moved or changed page, tell the user instead of retrying with another tab. Only close the tab the user explicitly asked to close.
close-tab only closes the tab shown in its confirmation. If it reports that there is no matching confirmation, nothing was closed: tell the user and let them ask again instead of calling close-tab again yourself.
